Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: No official Djibouti tax e-filing/e-payment portal evidence was found in gathered sources; World Bank 2025 press release discusses improving tax administration and "better access to e-services" but does not confirm an existing tax portal. Searched: "Hôtel des Impôts Djibouti e-tax portal", "e-filing Djibouti", "tax online payment Djibouti". ([World Bank press release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2025/01/16/new-project-will-help-djibouti-enhance-public-finance-and-develop-digital-services))
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: World Bank's 2024 GovTech case study on Djibouti's ASYCUDAWorld customs digitisation confirms a new tax administration IT system is 'under implementation' and slated for future integration into the government's X-ROAD interoperability platform. The January 2025 World Bank Economic and Financial Governance Project ($20m IDA grant) is explicitly designed to strengthen tax administration and citizen access to e-services, but no live online tax e-filing/e-payment portal was confirmed as operational. Score changed from 0/Unknown (no source) to 3/Under development on the basis of these two primary World Bank sources.
revised_comments: Djibouti's General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) does not yet operate a live online tax e-filing and e-payment portal. A new tax administration IT system is under implementation as part of the World Bank-financed Economic and Financial Governance Project (approved January 2025) and the earlier Public Administration Modernisation Project, which are building an interoperable government platform intended eventually to support online tax filing and payment.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: No evidence found that Djibouti's domestic IPS (SYRAD) has cross-border instant payment linkages; UNCDF assessment highlights cross-border remittance corridors and recommends improving interoperability and gateways, but does not indicate operational cross-border instant payment infrastructure. Searched for PAPSS participation Djibouti and SYRAD cross-border linkage; no confirmation found. ([UNCDF Migrant Money – Djibouti Infrastructure Assessment](https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Djibouti-Infrastructure-Assessment-Report-ENG.pdf))
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: PAPSS's own June 2026 network coverage map lists Djibouti among the countries with live PAPSS participants able to send and receive instant cross-border payments, corroborated by the Central Bank of Djibouti's 2022 Annual Report describing completion of integration work linking Djibouti's SYRAD platform to PAPSS and to COMESA's REPSS regional payment system. Score changed from 0/Unknown (no source) to 4/Partially functional. Flagged for human review as only participant-level status (not transaction volumes or corridor breadth) is confirmed, and the original 'no evidence found' conclusion was reached without checking PAPSS's own participant directory.
revised_comments: Djibouti is a live participant on the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), the continental instant cross-border payment infrastructure, following integration work by the Central Bank of Djibouti linking its domestic settlement platform (SYRAD) to PAPSS and to COMESA's REPSS regional payment system. Banks connected to PAPSS can settle instant cross-border payments in local currency with other PAPSS-live countries including Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Zambia, Nigeria and others.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No primary legal text was found in sources gathered that explicitly states mandatory data breach notification requirements in Djibouti's new Digital Code/data protection framework; secondary commentary indicates a comprehensive data protection law but the available sources reviewed did not provide a confirmable breach-notification obligation text. Searched: "Djibouti Digital Code data breach notification", "CNDP notification violation", "Djibouti personal data breach obligation". ([Techhive Advisory overview](https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-djiboutis-data-protection-law))
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Djibouti's Digital Code (Law No. 019/AN/23/9th L), enacted June 2025, contains explicit mandatory breach-notification provisions (Articles 14, 15, 407, 408): controllers must notify the CNDP within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach, and notify affected data subjects without undue delay where the breach poses a high risk. Score changed from 0/Unknown (no source) to 3/Mandatory on the basis of the primary legislative text (fetched and read) and Techhive Advisory's legal review, which the original researcher had cited but not read closely enough to extract the notification obligation.
revised_comments: Djibouti's Digital Code (Law No. 019/AN/23/9th L), enacted in June 2025, imposes a mandatory data breach notification regime on data controllers and processors, including payment service providers. Controllers must notify the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP) within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach unless it is unlikely to pose a risk, and must notify affected data subjects without undue delay where the breach poses a high risk to their rights and freedoms. Failure to notify is a criminal offence under the Code.

Comments: No public, periodic payment-system performance reporting (monthly/quarterly/annual statistics on SYRAD/RTGS/ACH) was found in gathered sources; Central Bank of Djibouti homepage references annual report and publications but does not provide payment system statistics on the page reviewed. Searched: "Banque Centrale de Djibouti statistiques systèmes de paiement SYRAD", "payment system report Djibouti". ([Central Bank of Djibouti](https://banque-centrale.dj))

revision_notes: The Central Bank of Djibouti (BCD) publishes a detailed Rapport Annuel each year with a dedicated chapter (Direction du Système et des Moyens de Paiement) reporting SYRAD transaction volumes and values, disaggregated by RTGS and ACH components, for the current and prior year. Score changed from 0/Unknown (no source) to 3/Annual on the basis of the BCD's 2023 and 2022 annual reports, both publicly available as PDFs on the BCD website — the original researcher had only checked the BCD homepage rather than its publications archive.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Djibouti publishes payment system operational statistics annually through its public Rapport Annuel, which includes a dedicated section from its payment and settlement systems directorate reporting SYRAD transaction volumes and values (split between the RTGS and Automated Clearing House components) for the reporting year alongside prior-year comparisons.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No public SYRAD rulebook/scheme rules were located via searches and the Central Bank of Djibouti website landing page did not provide scheme rules or rulebooks for SYRAD (only a news item referencing cheque rejection to SYRAD). Searched: "SYRAD rulebook", "Système de Règlement Automatisé de Djibouti règles", BCD publications. ([Central Bank of Djibouti](https://banque-centrale.dj))
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The BCD publishes on its website a description of SYRAD's objectives, eligible participants, membership conditions (signature of an adhesion agreement, technical certification) and operating principles, and the underlying Payment Systems Law (Loi n°118/AN/15/7ème L, 2015), which requires each system operator to establish written governance/risk rules, is publicly available via the official gazette (eJO) and the BCD site. No full downloadable SYRAD rulebook or pricing schedule was located. Score changed from 0/Unknown (no source) to 2/Partial - On Request on the basis of these BCD and gazette sources, which the original researcher's search terms did not surface.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Djibouti publishes key operating principles, eligibility criteria and membership conditions for its automated settlement system (SYRAD) on its official website, and the National Payment System Law (Law No. 118/AN/15/7th L of 2015) — which requires each payment system operator to establish written governance, risk-management and participation rules — is publicly available via the official gazette. A complete, downloadable SYRAD scheme rulebook with pricing and technical specifications was not identified, indicating partial rather than fully public availability of scheme rules.
